title: Historical Crude Oil Production and Hydrocarbon Extraction Dynamics in Venezuela (1970–2026)
authors: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) & U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
journal: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin (ASB), OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report (MOMR), and U.S. EIA International Energy Statistics
findings: 1970 Historical Peak: Conventional crude production peaked at 3,708 kb/d (OPEC ASB Table 3.5) / 3,754 kb/d (U.S. EIA crude + lease condensate).
1976 Nationalization: Formation of Petroleos de Venezuela S.A. (PDVSA); production regulated at ~2,294–2,345 kb/d under strict conservation ceilings.
1985 Glut Trough: Production contracted to 1,677 kb/d during global oil glut and OPEC quota constraints before the 1986 netback pricing collapse.
1998 Pre-Chavez Peak: Production expanded to 3,134 kb/d (OPEC Direct Communication) / 3,167 kb/d (U.S. EIA) under the Apertura Petrolera IOC joint ventures.
2002–2003 Paro Petrolero (General Strike): Output collapsed sharply in late 2002 / early 2003 to <1,500 kb/d monthly, averaging 2,604 kb/d in 2002 and 2,335 kb/d in 2003.
2013 Maduro Transition: Production stabilized on an observational plateau of 2,354 kb/d (OPEC Secondary Sources) and 2,389 kb/d (OPEC Direct Communication).
2017–2019 Sanctions & Macro Collapse: Output dropped precipitously following U.S. financial sanctions (EO 13808) and oil embargo (EO 13850), reaching 1,013 kb/d in 2019.
2020 Pandemic & Secondary Sanctions Nadir: Output plummeted to 512 kb/d (OPEC Secondary Sources annual average; mid-2020 monthly low of 392 kb/d).
2024–2026 Rebound: Production rebounded to 867 kb/d in 2024 (secondary) / 928 kb/d (direct), rising to ~955–1,081 kb/d in 2025 and ~990–1,095 kb/d in 2026 under OFAC GL 41/44.
verbatim_quote: "Crude oil production in Venezuela reached its historical peak in 1970 at 3,708 thousand barrels per day (tb/d). Following the restructuring under the Organic Law and subsequent market cycles, Venezuela produced 3,134 tb/d in 1998, averaging 2,354 tb/d in 2013 according to secondary sources (2,389 tb/d direct communication). Between 2015 and 2020, output declined by over 78% to an annual low of 512 tb/d in 2020 (secondary sources), before recovering to 867 tb/d in 2024 and surpassing 1.0 mb/d in 2025–2026 under authorized joint venture operations."
